summary: 米森重新审视人类语言起源的研究，认为音乐、情感和祖先的交流方式长期被低估。他以关于原始语言的不同设想把这些线索串在一起。

paragraphs.brief: 关于语言起源和演变的理论多年来一直是我研究的一个主要领域。
sentences: Theories on the origin and evolution of language have been a major area of my research for many years.
关于语言起源和演变的理论多年来一直是我研究的一个主要领域。
By 1859, when British scientist Charles Darwin published The Origin of Species, there was already a great deal of interest in this subject.
1859年，当英国科学家查尔斯·达尔文发表《物种起源》时，人们已经对此主题产生了极大的兴趣。
However, the debate became plagued by strange theories, so much so that in 1866 the influential Société de Linguistique de Paris banned all discussions about the origin of language.
然而，这场辩论被奇怪的理论所困扰，以至于在1866年，有影响力的巴黎语言学会禁止关于语言起源的一切讨论。
The ban lasted for more than a century, before a surge of research began during the 1990s.
禁令持续了一个多世纪，在1990年代开始大量研究之前。
Linguists, psychologists, anthropologists and archaeologists now frequently debate the origin of language and have published many articles and books on this topic.
语言学家、心理学家、人类学家和考古学家现在经常讨论语言的起源，并发表了许多关于这一主题的文章和书籍。
And yet, despite almost frenzied activity, limited progress has been made.
然而，尽管活动几乎疯狂，但进展有限。

paragraphs.brief: 迄今为止，许多理论都依赖于大脑大小与语言能力之间的假定联系，而没有认识到由此产生的问题：化石证据表明，尼安德特人的大脑比现代人、智人还要大，但考古证据表明尼安德特人缺乏语言能力。
sentences: I believe there are four reasons for this.
我认为这有四个原因。
The first is an insufficient concern with the archaeological and fossil proof of the brains and behaviour of our human ancestors.
第一，对人类祖先的大脑和行为的考古和化石证明不够关注。

Many theories to date rely on an assumed association between brain size and language abilities, without acknowledging the problem this creates: fossil evidence indicates that the Neanderthals had larger brains than modern humans, Homo sapiens, but archaeological evidence indicates that the Neanderthals lacked a capacity for language.
迄今为止，许多理论都依赖于大脑大小与语言能力之间的假定联系，而没有认识到由此产生的问题：化石证据表明，尼安德特人的大脑比现代人、智人还要大，但考古证据表明尼安德特人缺乏语言能力。
So something is seriously amiss with those theories.
所以这些理论有问题。

paragraphs.brief: 另一个是著名的民族音乐学家约翰·布莱辛，1973年的书《音乐是人吗？》，提出了音乐是固有和普遍人性的观点。
sentences: That 'something' might relate to the second reason for limited progress: insufficient concern with the other major aural and vocal communication system of modern humans: music.
“某种”可能与进展有限的第二个原因有关：对现代人其他主要的声响交流系统(音乐)的关心不够。

Even though the Société de Linguistique de Paris had nothing to say about studying the origin of music, academics appear to have had a self-imposed ban, with limited discussion of this issue during the 19th and 20th centuries.
尽管巴黎语言学会对研究音乐的起源没有任何意见，但学者们似乎在19世纪和20世纪期间对该问题只进行了有限的讨论。
However, there are notable exceptions that should be acknowledged.
但是，有一些值得注意的例外，应予以承认。
One is the aforementioned Charles Darwin who, in his 1871 book on human evolution, The Descent of Man, devoted several pages to the development of music.
其中一个是上述查尔斯·达尔文，他在1871年关于人类进化的书《人类的起源》中，用几页篇幅专门论述音乐的发展。
Another is the renowned ethnomusicologist John Blacking, whose 1973 book, How Musical is Man?, broached the idea that music is an inherent and universal human quality.
另一个是著名的民族音乐学家约翰·布莱辛，1973年的书《音乐是人吗？》，提出了音乐是固有和普遍人性的观点。

paragraphs.brief: 音乐的起源值得同语言的起源一样受到重视，因为我们不能没有语言就对待一种音乐。
sentences: The origin of music deserves as much attention as that of language, as we cannot treat one without the other.
音乐的起源值得同语言的起源一样受到重视，因为我们不能没有语言就对待一种音乐。
Those writers who had evidently annoyed the Société de Linguistique de Paris were quite aware of this.
那些显然惹恼巴黎语言学会的作家都很清楚这一点。
For them, music and language were intimately linked; the French writer and philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau's On the Origin of Language (1781) was a reflection on both music and language.
对他们来说，音乐和语言是紧密相连的；法国作家和哲学家让-雅克·罗梭的《语言起源》(1781年)对音乐和语言都进行了反思。
In contrast, Morten Christiansen and Simon Kirby's book, Language Evolution (2000), which they conceived as 'a definitive book on the subject', failed to mention music in any of its 17 chapters.
反之，莫滕·克里斯蒂安森和西蒙·柯比的书《语言演变(2000年)》在17章中都没有提到音乐。
Those authors have an important lesson to learn from Rousseau and other writers of his time who addressed the origin of language.
作者们可以从罗梭和他时代讲语言起源的其他作家那里学到重要的经验教训。

paragraphs.brief: 音乐是人类社会的一个普遍特征，在所有个人生活中发挥着重要作用。
sentences: Music is a universal feature of human society and plays a significant role in the lives of all individuals.
音乐是人类社会的一个普遍特征，在所有个人生活中发挥着重要作用。

Indeed, music is perhaps in even greater need of study than language: the latter has a self-evident function—the transmission of information—and can be readily accepted as a product of evolution, even if its specific evolutionary history remains unclear.
事实上，音乐比语言更需要学习：语言具有不言自明的功能——传递信息——并且可以很容易地被接受为进化的产物，即使其具体的进化历史仍然不明确。
But what is the point of music?
但音乐有什么意义？

paragraphs.brief: 这助长了对音乐的忽视，这反过来又限制了我们对语言的理解。
sentences: That question leads directly to a third reason for our lack of progress in understanding how language evolved, and indeed the human mind in general: an insufficient concern with emotion.
这个问题直接导致第三个原因，即我们在理解语言如何演变以及人类整体思想方面缺乏进展：对情绪的关心不够。
If music is about anything, it is about expressing emotion.
如果音乐是关于什么的，它就是表达情感。
But while archaeologists have put significant effort into examining the intellectual capacities of our ancestors, their emotional lives have been sorely neglected.
但是，虽然考古学家在研究我们祖先的智力能力方面作出了重大努力，但他们的感情生活却被严重忽视。
This has contributed to the neglect of music, which, in turn, has constrained our understanding of language.
这助长了对音乐的忽视，这反过来又限制了我们对语言的理解。

paragraphs.brief: 进展有限还有一个原因：那些对语言演变最具影响力的人完全搞错了，误导了其他人。
sentences: There is one further reason why progress has been limited: those who have been most influential regarding the evolution of language have simply got it wrong, and misled everyone else.
进展有限还有一个原因：那些对语言演变最具影响力的人完全搞错了，误导了其他人。

Linguist Derek Bickerton has made an important contribution towards our understanding of the origin of language by bringing his profound knowledge of linguistics to the discussions that have occurred.
语言学家德里克·比克顿通过将语言知识的深奥带入已经进行的讨论，为我们理解语言的起源作出了重要贡献。
But Bickerton's idea that the precursor of modern language consisted of words strung together with limited, if any, grammar is, I believe, fundamentally mistaken.
但是Bickerton认为现代语言的前身是由词串和有限的语法组成的我认为根本上是错误的

Bickerton refers to this precursor as 'proto-language' and suggests that it was similar to the type of language spoken by young children today, and mastered by apes through the use of computer keyboards.
比克顿把这种语言的前身称为“原始语言”，认为它类似于今天幼儿说的语言，也类似于类人猿通过电脑键盘所掌握的那种语言。
This idea has dominated the field of language origins for the last two decades, and is one that I once found persuasive.
过去二十年来，这一想法一直主导着语言起源领域，我曾经认为这一想法很有说服力。
But I now understand that it is not only flawed but has severely limited the progress that should have been made.
但我现在理解，这不仅有缺陷，而且严重限制了本应该取得的进展。

paragraphs.brief: 对Wray来说，原语言在语义上是复杂的，在语法上也是复杂的。
sentences: My book therefore provides an alternative view, one that draws on the ideas of a linguist who has, I believe, identified the true nature of proto-language.
因此，我的书提供了另一种观点，它借鉴了一位语言学家的想法，我认为，他已经确定了原语言的真正性质。
Her name is Alison Wray.
她叫艾莉森·赖
She argues that proto-language was 'holistic' rather than compositional in character.
她认为原语在性格上是“整体”而非构成性的。

By this she means that the precursor to language was a communication system composed of 'messages' rather than words; each message was uniquely associated with an arbitrary meaning, as are the utterances of language today.
她的意思是，语言的前身是由“信息”而不是文字组成的通信系统；每个信息都与任意的含义有着独特的联系，今天的语言的发音也是如此。

But in Wray's proto-language, they were not composed out of smaller units of meaning (i.e. words) which could be combined together using a rule system (i.e. grammar) to make more complex messages with emergent meanings.
但是在Wray的原版语言中，它们不是由较小的意义单位(即文字)组成的，这些单位可以使用规则系统(即语法)合并，使信息更复杂，具有紧急意义。
For Wray, proto-language was semantically complex and agrammatical.
对Wray来说，原语言在语义上是复杂的，在语法上也是复杂的。
I believe this insight enables us to understand the origin of music as well as language, and to relate both to the emotional lives of our human ancestors.
我相信，这种洞察力使我们能够理解音乐和语言的起源，并且能够与我们人类祖先的情感生活联系起来。

items.en: In the first paragraph, what does the writer suggest about the origin of language?
items.zh: 在第一段中，作者对语言的起源有何建议？
correct: The lack of progress is surprising given the amount of work being done.
鉴于正在做大量的工作，缺乏进展是令人吃惊的。

items.en: What is the ‘problem’ referred to in the second paragraph?
items.zh: 第二段中提到的 " 问题 " 是什么？
correct: Some current theories are based on conflicting evidence.
目前的一些理论是基于相互矛盾的证据。

items.en: What does the writer suggest about Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s work in 1781?
items.zh: 作者对让-雅克·卢梭在1781年的工作有何看法？
correct: Modern theorists should pay more attention to his approach.
现代理论家应该更加注意他的做法。

items.en: What is the writer’s current view of Derek Bickerton’s ideas?
items.zh: 作者目前对德里克·比克顿的想法有何看法？
correct: The assumption behind them is wrong.
他们背后的假设是错误的。

items.zh: 作者最后总结说，Alison Wray的想法将有助于在以下两点之间建立联系：

lead: The archaeologist Stephen Mithen talks about the ideas behind his new book on the origin of language.
考古学家史蒂芬·米森谈到他关于语言起源的新书背后的想法
